title: Third Party Risk Manager
description: As Mercury prepares to become a bank, our Third Party Risk Management (TPRM) program is in active development to meet bank-level regulatory expectations. As an early member of a growing TPRM team, you’ll help run the program day-to-day and contribute how it matures, bringing your own judgment and point of view to a function that is usually more rigidly defined, with room to be creative and make your mark. As a Third Party Risk Manager, you’ll help protect Mercury, our customers, and the broader financial ecosystem from the risks that come with relying on third parties. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Third Party Risk Management, you’ll complete third-party risk assessments, support risk reporting, and provide second-line oversight. As a Third Party Risk Manager, you will play a key part in helping protect Mercury, our customers, and the broader financial ecosystem from the risks associated with third parties. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Third Party Risk Management, you will conduct third party risk assessments, help build out related risk reporting, and carry out second line oversight activities to help reduce the impact of third-party risks. This position focuses on enterprise-wide TPRM, rather than in-depth expertise in a specific domain like security or privacy. You will work closely with subject-matter experts across Compliance, Information Security, Privacy, and Procurement to make sure their requirements are reflected in the program, bringing a view across the full third-party lifecycle and the regulatory expectations that come with banking.* Key Responsibilities: Assess and risk rate: Complete third-party risk assessments, risk rate third parties, and open and track issues through resolution.  Second-line oversight: Review and challenge first-line due diligence and ongoing monitoring, including reporting, approvals and oversight of those activities. First-line owners remain accountable for managing the third-party relationship, including SLAs, business reviews, exit strategies and onboarding. Reporting and data: Support maintenance of third party risk reporting and metrics for management and governance forums, and help keep the underlying data accurate. Tooling and automation: Help implement tooling and automation to make processes more efficient Program uplift: Support and contribute to uplift efforts across the TPRM program, including updates to policies, due diligence, risk assessment processes, and risk management across the third party lifecycle Required Qualifications: 4+ years of third party risk management experience, including 2+ years in a regulated financial services environment (bank, or fintech working with bank partners) Working knowledge of regulatory guidance on third party risk, including the Interagency Guidance on Third Party Relationships (and related FFIEC, OCC and FDIC expectations), and TPRM industry practices across the third party lifecycle (planning, due diligence, contracting, monitoring, termination) Hands-on experience completing third party risk assessments across multiple risk domains, not only security Experience reviewing and challenging first-line risk work with evidence-based pushback Experience supporting audits or exams of a TPRM program (gathering evidence, responding to requests, following up on findings) Experience building or maintaining TPRM reporting and metrics, with attention to data accuracy Solid program and project management skills, with experience supporting a program that spans multiple cross-functional components and driving process improvements through to implementation Proven ability to influence cross-functional partners (Procurement, Finance, InfoSec, Legal, Privacy) without direct authority Clear communicator who can explain a risk position and hold it under pushback Preferred Qualifications: Experience at a bank, or a fintech moving toward banking Experience improving or uplifting an existing TPRM program Experience with TPRM tooling, automation or AI-enabled workflows Familiarity with enterprise risk concepts (risk register, risk appetite, committee reporting) Relevant certification (e.g., CISA, CGRC) *Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. title: Senior Risk Officer
description: Blockchain is connecting the world to the future of finance. As the most trusted and fastest-growing global crypto company, it helps millions of people worldwide safely access cryptocurrency. Since its inception in 2011, Blockchain has earned the trust of over 90 million wallet holders and more than 40 million verified users, facilitating over $1 trillion in crypto transactions. We’re looking for a Senior Risk Officer to help build and run risk management across Blockchain.com. This is a company-wide role: you'll help identify, measure, and manage risk across our business lines, working closely with Compliance, Legal, Finance, Product, and Operations to strengthen our overall risk posture as we continue to scale and expand our business. A key part of this role is supporting our expansion into regulated derivatives. Blockchain.com already offers millions of customers a trusted way to buy, sell, and hold crypto, and we're extending those offerings into regulated futures and derivatives markets in the U.S. and other jurisdictions. You'll help build out the risk management program for that and other regulated derivatives entities, working alongside their compliance and risk officers to make sure risk is identified, monitored, and escalated appropriately as the business grows. You'll report into our broader Risk function and partner with senior leadership across the company to shape how we manage risk—from market, credit, and liquidity risk to operational, technology, and counterparty risk—while bringing specialized attention to the unique risks of our regulated derivatives activities. If you've built or run risk programs at a financial institution and want to apply that experience across a global crypto platform, this is the perfect opportunity for you. WHAT YOU WILL DO Help design, implement, and administer risk management frameworks, policies, and controls across the company's business lines Identify, measure, monitor, and report on key risk categories, including market, credit, liquidity, operational, technology, legal, and counterparty risk Establish and maintain risk tolerance limits, monitor for breaches, and escalate issues to senior management and governance committees as needed Support the risk management program for the firm's regulated derivatives entities, covering areas such as customer fund segregation, margin and collateral adequacy, capital risk, and settlement risk Partner with the business’s compliance function and regulatory counsel to ensure risk controls meet applicable regulatory expectations across the jurisdictions in which the firm operates Help oversee risk related to digital asset collateral, including valuation, haircuts, custody arrangements, and liquidation triggers Prepare and deliver regular risk exposure reporting to senior management, risk committees, and, where applicable, regulators and self-regulatory organizations Partner with Product and Engineering to assess and manage risk as new products and features are launched Support business continuity, disaster recovery, and operational resilience planning Contribute to the annual review and testing of risk management programs and controls, and help track remediation of identified gaps Advise senior leadership on emerging risks as the business and its product offerings evolve, including in fast-moving areas like crypto derivatives WHAT YOU WILL NEED 8+ years of risk management experience at a financial institution, broker-dealer, futures firm, exchange, or similar regulated entity Strong working knowledge of core risk disciplines—market, credit, liquidity, and operational risk—and how they apply in practice Experience building, implementing, or enhancing a risk management program or framework Excellent judgment and the confidence to make sound risk calls in a fast-moving, evolving business Clear, plain-English communication skills–you can explain risk concepts to engineers, executives, and regulators alike Comfort working across a wide range of stakeholders and business lines in a company supporting multiple regulated activities NICE TO HAVE Experience with futures, derivatives, or FCM risk management, including customer fund segregation, margin, and collateral risk Experience supporting a new regulated entity through registration, licensing, or similar regulatory processes Familiarity with crypto or digital asset products and their associated risks Experience with enterprise risk management programs spanning multiple business lines or entities Familiarity with risk considerations across multiple regulatory regimes and jurisdictions COMPENSATIONS & PERKS Competitive salary and meaningful equity in an industry-leading company. title: Senior Manager, Financial Reporting & Technical Accounting
description: For over 30 years, Angi has powered the future of the home services industry, creating an environment where homeowners and pros benefit from more jobs done well. For homeowners, our platform is a reliable way to find skilled pros. For pros, we're a reliable business partner who helps them find the winnable work they want, when they want. For employees, we're an amazing place to call home. We can't wait to welcome you. Angi at a glance: Founded in 1995 as Angie’s List and rebranded in 2021 Global company with 9 brands in 8 countries and employees worldwide Homeowners have turned to us for 300 million home projects and counting Job Summary Angi is seeking a highly motivated and experienced Senior Manager of Financial Reporting and Technical Accounting to join our accounting team. This critical role will be responsible for providing technical accounting expertise, ensuring compliance with US GAAP, and supporting the Company's financial reporting process. The ideal candidate will possess a strong understanding of accounting principles, excellent analytical skills, and the ability to effectively communicate complex accounting issues to both technical and non-technical audiences. Key Responsibilities SEC Reporting Steward and manage the preparation and filing of all SEC reports, including Forms 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, and proxy statements, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and adherence to regulatory deadlines. Lead the drafting, review, and continuous improvement of MD&A, footnote disclosures, and earnings press releases in coordination with Legal, IR, and executive leadership. Manage the XBRL tagging process and maintain all EDGAR submissions. Stay current on evolving SEC rules, comment letter trends, and disclosure best practices, proactively updating disclosures to reflect new guidance. Serve as the primary point of contact for external auditors on all SEC reporting and technical accounting matters. Technical Accounting Serve as Angi's subject matter expert on US GAAP, providing authoritative guidance on complex and judgmental accounting areas including revenue recognition (ASC 606), equity compensation (ASC 718), leases (ASC 842), business combinations, goodwill, and debt instruments. Research, document, and communicate accounting positions on new transactions, product initiatives, and strategic deals, ensuring alignment with auditors and senior leadership. Develop and maintain company-wide accounting policies and ensure consistent application across the organization. Monitor and assess the impact of new and proposed accounting standards (FASB/SEC), preparing implementation plans and communicating implications to key stakeholders. Internal Controls & SOX Compliance Oversee and strengthen the SOX control environment related to financial reporting, including control design, documentation, testing, and remediation activities. Partner with internal audit and external auditors to support efficient, high-quality audits and reviews. Ensure the adequacy and effectiveness of disclosure controls and procedures. People Leadership & Cross-Functional Partnership Recruit, manage, mentor, and develop a team of accounting professionals, fostering a culture of excellence, accountability, and continuous growth. Act as a strategic advisor to the Controller and CFO on the accounting implications of complex transactions, strategic initiatives, and emerging business decisions. Partner with FP&A, Legal, Tax, and Corporate Accounting to align on disclosures, transactions, and accounting conclusions. Drive scalability and efficiency through process improvements, automation, and systems enhancements across the reporting and close cycle through the use of AI. Qualifications Required 8-10 years of progressive accounting experience, with substantial time in SEC reporting and technical accounting at a public company and/or Big 4 public accounting firm. CPA required. Deep, demonstrable knowledge of US GAAP and SEC reporting requirements, with hands-on experience across multiple complex accounting areas. Proven track record of managing and developing a team of accounting professionals. Strong experience with SOX compliance, including designing, maintaining, and evaluating internal controls over financial reporting. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex accounting matters for non-accounting audiences including the Board, Audit Committee, and executive team. Experience with Workiva and EDGAR filing systems. Preferred Experience in a marketplace, technology, or two-sided platform business. Background in a high-growth, publicly traded company environment with increasing reporting complexity. Familiarity with NetSuite or comparable ERP systems. Experience presenting to or preparing materials for an Audit Committee. Compensation & Benefits The base salary band for this position ranges from $120,000 - $195,000, commensurate with experience and performance. Compensation may vary based on factors such as geographic location. This position will be eligible for a competitive year end performance bonus Full medical, dental, vision package to fit your needs Flexible vacation policy; work hard and take time when you need it Pet discount plans & retirement plan with company match (401K) The rare opportunity to work with sharp, motivated teammates solving some of the most unique challenges and changing the world We value diversity We know that the best ideas come from teams where diverse points of view uncover new solutions to hard problems. We welcome and value individuals who bring diverse life experiences, educational backgrounds, cultures, and work experiences. Our hiring process may utilize artificial intelligence (AI) tools to assist in candidate screening and assessment. Our AI tools are designed to complement, not replace, human decision-making. #LI-Remote

title: Sr. Manager, Security — Continuous Monitoring v 2.0
description: RDQ227R1175 While candidates in the listed location(s) are encouraged for this role, candidates in other locations will be considered. About Databricks Databricks is the data and AI company. More than 12,000 organizations worldwide — including Comcast, Condé Nast, Grammarly, and over 50% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform to unify and democratize data, analytics and AI. Databricks is headquartered in San Francisco, with offices around the globe and was founded by the original creators of Lakehouse, Apache Spark™, Delta Lake and MLflow. About the Team The Continuous Monitoring (ConMon) team at Databricks builds and operates the engineering infrastructure that keeps Databricks' security control posture visible, measurable, and defensible at all times. We build automation that continuously assesses whether security controls are actually working across cloud environments, SaaS platforms, identity systems, and enterprise applications — surfacing drift, coverage gaps, and control failures as they happen rather than at the next audit. Our work sits at the intersection of security engineering and GRC: we turn control requirements into code, evidence collection into automation, and security posture into intelligence that drives decisions. The ConMon team also maintains security tooling and scanning infrastructure to aid control evaluation. This includes scanning for secret leaks, asset vulnerabilities, and SAST. As Databricks' security program, cloud footprint, and regulatory obligations all scale, the Continuous Monitoring team is responsible for ensuring the company's control posture is always verifiable, always current, and never a surprise. The Role Databricks is looking for a Senior Manager to lead the Continuous Monitoring team. You will own the engineering function that measures whether Databricks' security controls are working — across cloud infrastructure, identity, SaaS, and enterprise systems — and turns that measurement into something the Security organization, and its auditors, can rely on. That includes demonstrating control posture against the frameworks the business carries (SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, PCI DSS, and emerging AI governance requirements), but the underlying question is broader: are the controls Databricks depends on actually in place and operating everywhere they are supposed to be? This is an engineering management role. The team writes production Python, operates data pipelines against cloud and SaaS APIs, and integrates with GRC and security tooling. Success is measured in control coverage, the accuracy and timeliness of what the team reports, and how quickly gaps get to the people who can close them. The role requires enough technical depth to review that work credibly, and enough judgement to prioritize the controls where measurement actually reduces risk. As the leader of Continuous Monitoring, you'll be responsible for growing and developing the team; setting a clear vision, priority, and strategy; making the case for the headcount and tooling the program needs; and building durable partnerships across GRC (SAC, SAF, Governance, Risk Management, TPRM), IT, Legal, and Engineering — the organizations that own the controls your team monitors. The Impact You Will Have Team Building & People Leadership Hire strong Security Software Engineers who bring genuine engineering skill to compliance automation. Support engineers in their career development with clear, specific feedback; develop senior ICs into technical leaders and grow the next generation of security engineering managers. Set and hold a high bar for engineering quality: code review standards, reliability and observability expectations for automation pipelines, and documentation that remains useful across audit cycles and team changes. Build a team that combines GRC domain knowledge with software engineering discipline, and hire for both. Control Measurement Program Ownership Own the strategy and roadmap for Databricks' continuous monitoring platform — control state collection at cloud scale, continuous posture assessment, security and GRC tooling integration, and remediation tracking. Define what the program measures and why: prioritize the controls whose failure would matter most to Databricks' security posture, rather than defaulting to the set a given framework happens to enumerate. Ensure coverage keeps pace with the business — new cloud environments, new products and services, new certifications and regulatory obligations, and AI governance controls that current tooling does not yet assess. Reduce manual evidence collection systematically; set and track targets for automated control coverage, freshness, and audit burden on Engineering teams. Own the accuracy of the team's output, including false positive rates; findings should be reliable enough that control owners act on them without re-verification. Posture Visibility & Executive Intelligence Own the security posture dashboard
